label: conj:two-filtration-bridge
title: Two-filtration bridge: iterated-integral depth $\leftrightarrow$ partition-cellular GB-depth via $e_\lambda$
html:
Conjecture. Two-filtration bridge: iterated-integral depth \leftrightarrow partition-cellular GB-depth via e_\lambda

Conjecture (two-filtration bridge: iterated-integral depth \leftrightarrow partition-cellular GB-depth via central idempotents).

The substrate convolution Hopf algebra \mathcal{H}_q carries two distinct filtrations:

  • the iterated-integral depth on grouplikes (depth correspondence), G^{(0)} \subseteq G^{(1)} \subseteq \cdots with G^{(n)} generated by \{\exp_q, \log_q, \mathrm{Li}_2^q, \ldots, \mathrm{Li}_n^q\};
  • the partition-cellular GB-depth on the centre Z(H_n(q)) (attributed to curvature-rank GB stratification, stratified \Phi_q — but the first stratifies by the curvature rank of words and supplies no partition-indexed filtration, so this conjecture presupposes the very word-to-partition step that is unestablished; see docs/audits/2026-08-16-three-gb-filtrations-one-name.md), Z^{(0)}(A) \subseteq Z^{(1)}(A) \subseteq \cdots where \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) = \max_\square h(\square).

These are different numbers — for the figure-8 self-conjugate cell \lambda = (2, 2), iterated-integral depth = 2 but partition GB-depth = 3 (max hook length). The conjecture: they are related, and the bridge is via the central primitive idempotents e_\lambda.

Statement

For each \lambda \vdash n, the central idempotent e_\lambda \in Z(H_n(q)) has a canonical iterated-integral depth lift \hat{e}_\lambda \in G^{(d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda))}(\mathcal{H}_q) where the depth d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) is given by:

  d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    2 & \text{if } \lambda \text{ is self-conjugate (amphichiral cell)} \\
    3 & \text{if } \lambda, \lambda' \text{ form a chiral pair} \\
    \min(\mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda), 2\,\lceil n/2 \rceil) & \text{otherwise}
  \end{cases}

and the bridge map is given by the action of e_\lambda on the depth-d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) component of \mathrm{Li}_n^q at the canonical Bring shape parameter for cell \lambda.

Structural justification of the statement

The two filtrations have orthogonal information:

  • Iterated-integral depth counts how many polylogarithm factors are needed to express a grouplike — equivalently, the Goncharov motivic-Galois weight.
  • Partition-cellular GB-depth counts how many braid generators are needed to express a Hecke element — equivalently, the Bruhat-length/cellular complexity.

They cannot be equal in general (different units; one counts "transcendental complexity," the other counts "algebraic combinatorial complexity"). But they are bridged by the central idempotents, which simultaneously:

  • live in Z(H_n(q)) at a specific GB-depth (max hook), and
  • pair under Markov trace with grouplikes at a specific iterated- integral depth.

The bridge map \lambda \mapsto d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) is what the conjecture predicts.

Concrete predictions

\lambda \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}} d_{\mathrm{II}} Period type witnessed
(2,2) self-conj. 3 2 \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \in \mathcal{P}_2^+
(3), (1,1,1) chiral pair 3 3 \mathrm{CS}(3_1) \in \mathcal{P}_3^-
(2, 1) self-conj. 3 2 hyperbolic vol if 3-mfd (not T(2,3) = 3_1)
(4) totally symm 4 2 sym-channel vol (depends on shape)
(2, 2, 1, \ldots) depends 2 if self-conj, 3 if pair \ldots

The general pattern: self-conjugacy under partition transpose \Rightarrow even iterated-integral depth (real period); chiral pair \Rightarrow odd depth (Tate-twisted period). Verifies rem:chirality-period-pairing.

Reduction to known structure

At n = 2, 3, 4: the table above can be checked exhaustively against the Hecke-cell structure. Self-conjugate partitions of small n are (1), (2,1) [no, (2,1) is its own transpose], (2,2), (3,2,1), \ldots (these are the partitions equal to their transpose, called self-conjugate). The bridge map gives them depth-2 witnesses; chiral pairs split into depth-3 witnesses.

At n \geq 5: the partition combinatorics gets richer; Hoefsmit seminormal form (prop:hoefsmit-seminormal-form) and the explicit e_\lambda formula (prop:explicit-central-idempotent) allow the bridge to be computed cell-by-cell.
